text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Malaysian government approves construction of a bridge to replace existing causeway linking Johor Baru and Singapore.
- Singapore has cme out tops in a regional honesty test conducted by the Readers Digest, with 9 out of 10 Singaporeans returning wallets to the supposed "owners".
- American Express has received approval from the Monetary Authority of Singapore to issue credit cards in Singapore.
- Asian stocks are in shock at the prospect of higher U.S. interest rates for the first time in two years, fund managers say.
- Global share and bond markets are jittery as the view that the US Federal Reserve with nudge up interest rates gains further ground.
The turnaround in top bids at recent state tenders suggests developers are expecting a gratual recovery in the private condominium market by late next year, analysts said.
- Housing loans for private residential property have picked up and bankers said most purchases were at prices not more than 10 percent below the peak.
- Creative Technology's "audio-centric" strategy of focusing on sound cards is paying of handsomely, chairman Sim Wong Hoo says.
- Malaysian Resources Corporation, which has iuterests in media, property and pwer generation, is expected to announce a "complex restructuring" today, a company official said.
